theory.title: Future perfect for actions completed by a future time
theory.explanation: Use will have + past participle to say that something will be completed before a point in the future: By 2030, the city will have built three new parks.
theory.tip: Future perfect = will have + participio; suele aparecer con by + fecha o momento futuro.

content.passage: The town has set ambitious environmental targets. By 2030, it will have planted ten thousand trees and built several new cycle routes. The council expects that most public buildings will have installed solar panels by then. Local schools will have introduced new environmental projects, too. The mayor says that these changes will not solve every problem, but they will have made the town cleaner and healthier.
